text.tspan: Set up VPC CNI custom networking in 5 steps
1 · Add a secondary CIDR to the VPC, and a pod subnet in EACH AZ your nodes use
aws ec2 associate-vpc-cidr-block --vpc-id vpc-0abc --cidr-block 100.64.0.0/16
2 · Turn on custom networking in aws-node (the VPC CNI pods)
AWS_VPC_K8S_CNI_CUSTOM_NETWORK_CFG=true
ENI_CONFIG_LABEL_DEF=topology.kubernetes.io/zone
3 · Create one ENIConfig per AZ, named after the AZ
us-west-1a → subnet: subnet-0pod1a, securityGroups: sg-0podtraffic
4 · Replace the nodes (old nodes keep the old set-up)
new node group → cordon and drain the old nodes
5 · Fix max pods (the primary ENI no longer hosts pods)
m5.large: 29 → 20 · prefix delegation gives far more
How a new node picks its ENIConfig
The node has the label topology.kubernetes.io/zone=us-west-1a
ENI_CONFIG_LABEL_DEF says: "use that label's value as the ENIConfig name"
ENIConfig us-west-1a → subnet-0pod1a + sg-0podtraffic
The CNI creates the node's secondary ENIs in that pod subnet
Max pods on an m5.large (3 ENIs, 10 IPs each)
Custom networking: (3 − 1) × (10 − 1) + 2 = 20
Prefix delegation: far more (AWS suggests a cap of 110 on small instances)
⚠ EKS managed add-on: put these settings in the add-on's configuration values.
kubectl set env can be overwritten by the next add-on update (two owners again).
Short terms
VPC = Virtual Private Cloud
CNI = Container Network Interface
ENI = Elastic Network Interface (a virtual network card)
CIDR = Classless Inter-Domain Routing (an IP range)
AZ = Availability Zone
EKS = Elastic Kubernetes Service
